origin: The previews record is right, but the post's $75M is above the $72M every trade reported. It misstates the record it predicts could fall: Endgame opened to $357.1M, not $365M. Its central claim, an opening "in the $345M range, probably more" with a possible record, was far above every published forecast on the fact sheet: Sony's $190M to $195M, trade estimates of $260M to $280M, a few estimates above $300M, and CNBC's "expected to ... remain behind Endgame". The $800M+ global figure is also well above Sony's $465M projection. Expected honest rating: 30 to 55.

evidence_up.evidence_note: Real. The Hollywood Reporter, Ryan Gajewski, "Spider-Man: Brand New Day Opening Beats Endgame for Box Office Record", published 2026-08-03 14:40 UTC, https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-news/spider-man-brand-new-day-opening-record-endgame-box-office-1236662986/ (src/thr-spiderman-record.md). Verbatim: "Sony Pictures‘ new movie earned $360 million from 4,487 North American screens in Monday actuals, which is up from the $355 million that the studio had projected on Sunday. This leaps past Avengers: Endgame’s previous record of $357.1 million in its domestic opening from April 2019". Also: "Brand New Day’s global weekend total stands at $932 million, meaning that Endgame still holds the record for the best worldwide opening weekend with $1.2 billion." The Sunday figure of $355 million and Sony's Sunday projection are in THR, 2026-08-02 15:18 UTC (src/thr-spiderman-sunday.md) and Deadline's Sunday edition (Wayback snapshot 20260802171823, src/deadline-spiderman-wayback-20260802171823.md).
pushes: New information that adds to the fact sheet: on Monday, August 3, 2026, final weekend figures showed Spider-Man: Brand New Day opened to $360 million in North America, up from the $355 million Sony had estimated on Sunday, passing Avengers: Endgame's $357.1 million for the biggest domestic opening weekend ever. Its global opening was $932 million, second only to Endgame's $1.2 billion. Does that change your rating?
